title: HYDRON RESILIENCE: SECURITY ASPECTS OF NETWORKS INTEROPERABILITY (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3A.240) EXPRO+
description: Objective:The objective of this study is to assess the feasibility of applying Common Criteria framework (or equivalent) to guarantee compatible security mechanisms with HydRON (High-throughput Optical Network).Targeted Improvements:To achieve security interoperability of HydRON with other networks with a clear protection profile definition in line with international standards.Description:Multiple constellations are expected to be developed in the coming years, addressing different applications, like navigation, Earth Observation and communications as well as defence. Each constellation will be optimized for the target application, in terms of technologies, coverage, but also security functions. The challenge, but also the opportunity is to make use of all the possible infrastructure to enhance coverage and resilience of these systems by the integration of optical communication security features like Low Probability to be detected or interfered (LPD/LPI).However, different users will have different protection profiles and thereforesecurity targets will differ between networks. The Common Criteria for Information Technology Security Evaluation (referred to as Common Criteria) is an international standard (ISO/IEC 15408) used to specify security functional and assurance requirements, to guarantee implementation and verification of the security features and it can be used as a baseline for the security analysis of different networks and interoperability of security levels.This activity shall define a set of protection profiles for different target users and identify the security targets for different networks. Taking HydRON as a baseline for communications, the activity shall consider additional, selected national or EC networks interconnected by optical links in space or with optical ground stations and ground networks.For such security interoperability, the activity will define the required security functions (confidentiality, integrity, availability, authentication, non-repudiation...) and achievable levels of assurance by the different space networks. For the sected networks, an analysis of the impact shall be performed for each of these security functions, including a preliminary assessment of vulnerabilities by different potential threat actors and its impact on the system. The feasibility of applying Common Criterialframework or similar framework for these networks shall be assessed. Additionally, the achievable level of protection by the different networks shall be provided as a draft catalogue, to be presented to potential users. The activity shall define initial access scenarios for Ministries of Defence (MODs) and Civil Security Entities to utilise the upcoming HydRON installation to conduct dedicated, potentially classified testingvalidating defencegrade security, resilience behaviours, and interoperability in realistic operational scenarios and providing inputs to preliminary vulnerability assessment analysing operational impacts of potential attacks.
